from pysat.solvers import Solver
from pysat.formula import CNF

# Graph definition
n_vertices = 34
n_colors = 4

edges = [
    (0,8), (0,12), (0,21), (0,28), (0,29), (0,30), (0,33), (1,17), (1,28), (1,31),
    (2,6), (2,18), (2,21), (2,26), (3,12), (3,18), (3,23), (3,33), (4,17), (4,19),
    (4,20), (4,21), (4,22), (4,24), (4,28), (4,32), (5,6), (5,10), (5,17), (5,19),
    (5,28), (6,16), (6,20), (6,27), (7,24), (7,27), (8,16), (8,18), (8,31), (9,19),
    (9,20), (9,26), (10,13), (10,14), (10,16), (10,20), (10,21), (10,26), (10,32),
    (11,14), (11,18), (11,23), (11,26), (11,30), (11,32), (12,14), (12,21), (12,22),
    (12,24), (12,30), (13,22), (13,24), (13,27), (14,17), (14,25), (14,27), (14,28),
    (14,31), (15,22), (15,23), (15,28), (15,31), (16,24), (16,25), (16,28), (16,32),
    (17,19), (17,25), (17,26), (17,29), (17,33), (18,21), (18,25), (18,33), (19,22),
    (19,23), (19,26), (19,28), (19,32), (20,22), (20,24), (20,27), (20,28), (21,26),
    (21,28), (22,23), (22,28), (23,24), (23,28), (23,31), (25,26), (25,27), (25,29),
    (25,30), (25,31), (25,33), (26,29), (26,32), (29,33), (30,32), (31,32)
]

# Variable encoding: var(v, c) = v * n_colors + c + 1
def var(v, c):
    return v * n_colors + c + 1

cnf = CNF()

# Each vertex must have at least one color
for v in range(n_vertices):
    cnf.append([var(v, c) for c in range(n_colors)])

# Each vertex has at most one color
for v in range(n_vertices):
    for c1 in range(n_colors):
        for c2 in range(c1+1, n_colors):
            cnf.append([-var(v, c1), -var(v, c2)])

# Adjacent vertices must have different colors
for (u, v) in edges:
    for c in range(n_colors):
        cnf.append([-var(u, c), -var(v, c)])

# Solve
solver = Solver(name='g3')
solver.append_formula(cnf)
result = solver.solve()

print(f"Satisfiable: {result}")

if result:
    model = solver.get_model()
    coloring = []
    for v in range(n_vertices):
        for c in range(n_colors):
            if var(v, c) in model:
                coloring.append(c)
                break
    print(f"Coloring: {coloring}")
    
    # Verify
    valid = True
    for (u, v) in edges:
        if coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
            print(f"Conflict at edge ({u},{v}): both have color {coloring[u]}")
            valid = False
    print(f"Valid coloring: {valid}")
